canonical_claim: The rebuild implementation reuses `discoverUniverse`, `foldManifestEdges`, `foldDeltasIntoGeneration`, `computeHeartbeatFloor`, and `prefixEligible` rather than adding a new scanner or merge machinery.
The generation-binding plan does not modify `contrib/aws`; all GCS behavior is implemented in ClickHouse's HTTP, object-storage, and CAS layers.

The view-side names are `Store::syncRetiredView()` and `CasEventType::RetiredViewAdvance` with event string `retired_view_advance`; the lease-side names `MountLeaseKeeper`, `renewOnce`, `mount_renew_period`, and `SingleWriterSlot` remain unchanged.

A different-content overwrite is not treated as a legitimate repoint because MergeTree parts are immutable and mutations mint new names; the intended republish path handles re-drive conflicts explicitly.
The Phase A plan deletes the copy-forward pre-pass and accepts the rare in-closure GET+PUT because the in-closure gate is idempotent under CAS retry.
The writer-side RetireView, syncer, observed_gc_round, and ack-floor are deleted only after all writer metadata point-read sites replace RetireView reads.

The rejected raw-body plan defined a per-hash `.meta` descriptor as a three-state `{clean, condemned, tombstone}` register whose etag is the sole linearization token, while blob bodies are raw immutable content and the writer-side `RetireView`, syncer, `observed_gc_round`, and ack-floor are removed.

The separate retired-set object family was removed in favor of kCondemned rows embedded in in-degree runs.; The current retired-in-snapshot refactor replaces the prose's three-cursor merge and separate `retired_refs` runs with a two-cursor source-edge merge, `kCondemned` sentinel rows, and a fold-seal `condemned_summary`.; The retired-in-snapshot design removes the `RetiredSet` object, `CART` magic, `Layout::retiredKey`, and `GcState::retired_refs`, and changes settlement from a three-cursor merge to a two-cursor merge.; The separate `RetiredSet` object family, `retiredKey`, `GcState::retired_refs`, `FormatId::RetiredSet`, and magic `CART` were deleted and the `CART` value is reserved never to be reused.
Removing the spare-side `scheduleMetaJob(... clearSparedMeta ...)` call requires no meta format change, no new I/O, and no delete-path change; `writeCondemnedMeta` and `deleteConfirmedMeta` remain.

The old `RootShardManifest`/`CasRootShardCodec` format has no compatibility scaffolding or dual-format reader: the CAS pool schema constant is bumped so old-format pools fail closed with a clear message through a pool-format bump, and every `RootShard` reference is deleted.
The deleted `RootShardManifest` codec tests are replaced by `gtest_cas_ref_codecs.cpp`, which covers canonical ID rendering/parsing, every ref operation kind, and ref log and snapshot validation.

The CAS stabilization iteration excludes large `CasGc.cpp` and `Cas::Store` structural refactors, new abstractions or configuration knobs without consumers, pre-emptive generality, and behavior changes justified only by taste.

The CAS fork uses three footprint rings: Ring 0 covers `ContentAddressed/` and `Core/`, Ring 1 covers CA-specific append-only lines in shared files, and Ring 2 covers shared upstream code that may be changed only when the delta shrinks, neutralizes, fixes, or simplifies the carried fork diff.

The `skip_access_check` fix reads the per-disk configuration directive in the CA factory; global `skip_access_check` plumbing through shared `IDisk::startupImpl` and generic `DiskSelector` isolation remain deferred Ring-2 work.
The stale `checkContentAddressedDiskRestrictions` no-op is removed from shared `MergeTreeData` because deleting it reduces the Ring-1 CA footprint rather than adding shared surface.
C5 is the only medium-risk behavioral change: it is a pure encapsulation of borrowed projection transactions, lands last with focused merge/mutate review, and can be reverted independently.

Removing `root_shards` and `fence_seq` is accepted because CAS is pre-release with no compatibility requirement; the affected pool-meta and GC-state codecs are covered by format tests and must have no remaining live consumers.

Changing run-file CRC coverage to include the block head, i.e. widening CRC coverage, changes the on-disk run-file framing; this is acceptable pre-release because run files are attempt-scoped and short-lived, old-format run files are never expected to survive, and writer and reader must be updated together.

The decommission design does not build a durable roster, does not auto-decommission inactive members, does not modify ReplicatedMergeTree ZooKeeper metadata, and provides no FORCE, per-namespace, or dry-run variant.
The rev.6 proposal specified a default `materialization_grace_ms` of 30000 ms for unclean handovers and no wait for a drained clean release.

The approved CAS codecs v3 design makes `docs/superpowers/cas/codecs_proposal_v3.md` the normative format reference and supersedes `codecs_proposal_v2.md`; `codecs.md` becomes a historical audit after `Formats/README.md` exists.
The refsnaplog conversion is a pre-release hard cutover with no legacy-binary-to-text dual-read fallback.
The blob-meta cutover deletes the `CAMT` binary codec in one pre-release commit and performs no binary-to-text dual read.
The streaming checksum changes the checksum value from the former one-shot `cityHash128(run_bytes)` algorithm because `object_cap = 0` forbids materializing a run for hashing.
The envelope uses a codec-local ref escaper that leaves `/` unchanged, escapes quotes, backslashes, and control characters, and makes byte-budget arithmetic independent of global JSON settings.
The source-layout refactoring includes the final renames `Cas::Store` → `Cas::Pool` and `Cas::Build` → `Cas::PartWriteTxn`, after layout and decomposition phases.

The refactoring fixes both dependency-direction violations rather than documenting around them; the backend-to-`CasTextFormat` violation disappears when v3 codecs own `sealObject` and `openObject`, so no `SealingBackend` decorator is planned.

The remaining post-v3 direction violation is `CasEvent.h` including the envelope header for `toEventKind`; the mapper is to move into `Formats/CasBlobEnvelopeFormat.h` so `CasEvent` can become dependency-free.
The refactoring merges files rather than classes, keeps type names and APIs unchanged during the merge phase, and places types/enums before codecs before logic in merged files.
Per-object `Formats/` files are deliberately not merged because their one-object-per-file organization is a settled codecs-v3 decision.
